prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and active peptide forms of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made incretin-based therapy of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B019 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The scientific case rests on a complete arc. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and incretin physiology, Drucker established the proglucagon-derived peptide biology and the gut and pancreatic actions, and Mojsov is credited with identifying and synthesizing the active truncated peptide. That arc has been confirmed over decades and in large independent randomized trials in type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal signals. The first round showed that all six of us reached the same configuration independently, but I do not count that as evidence. The case stands on originality, maturity and the consequences for patients, and none of the first-round statements weakened any of the three. The citation is worded around physiology and active peptide forms, so it does not claim liraglutide, semaglutide or the drug class.
statement.case_against: The weakness is attribution, and round 1 did not remove it. The three-person limit excludes Lotte Bjerre Knudsen, whose medicinal chemistry made a short-lived peptide into a usable drug, and that exclusion has a cost I will not call neutral. Mojsov's precedence over the Habener group on the active GLP-1(7-36) form is contested. Habener is not on the supplied credit list and I cannot verify priority from the material available to me, so my confidence in the third place rests on recollection and on the candidate record. B002 has the cleanest credit on the shortlist (Walter and Mori) and would be fully defensible. If the Mojsov claim proved no stronger than the Habener claim, I would move to B002 before I would substitute Knudsen, because that substitution would change the citation from discovery to development. A further weakness is that the long-term safety and durability of incretin therapy are still being characterized.

responses.point: Linnarsson would openly weigh Knudsen for the third B019 place if the Habener dispute proved unresolvable, and suggested that discovery and drug development may be better treated as separate recognitions.
responses.response: I understand the reasoning and I accept the conditional. Where I differ is on what Knudsen would replace. If Mojsov's claim fails, the discovery-side citation loses its third pillar, and adding Knudsen then produces a mixed citation that is neither clean physiology nor clean development. In that case I would go to B002 instead. Splitting B019 into two parts would not help because the cap leaves too few places for Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen together, and a second part would also raise the question why one achievement is given two parts and another none. So I do not support separate recognitions as a remedy. The honest course is to state the exclusion in our deliberation and to word the citation so that it does not claim the drugs.

responses.point: Perlmann asked why the credit problem in B004 is more tolerable than in B002 and said B002 offers a cleaner two-person credit if B019 attribution cannot be settled.
responses.response: The question is fair and I answer it directly. B004 has six names with no defensible trio, which is why I fall back on it last of the three. B002 is a strong fallback and I rank it first among my alternatives for the reason you give. I disclose again that you and I are frequent co-authors, none of it on a shortlisted candidate. I have also dropped my opening B004 trio of Deisseroth, Hegemann and Miesenböck. El-Manira and you are right that substituting Miesenböck for Nagel separates the molecular finding from its discoverers, and I cannot defend that trio against the objection. My willingness to move to B002 is tied to a specific condition: the Mojsov claim must be shown to be no better than the competing claim. Unresolved dispute alone, with the record unchanged since the opening round, is not enough for me.

responses.point: El-Manira ranked B002 first in the opening round for its conceptual originality and clean Walter and Mori credit, moved B019 to the top in round 1, and noted that early clinical translation matters less for a basic-mechanism prize.
responses.response: I accept your point that early translation is not a defect in a basic-mechanism prize, and I withdraw the suggestion that clinical scale should settle the comparison by itself. I still place B019 first, because the question is how well the discovery and its consequences are established, and here the discovery-side work is both original and demonstrated in patients. On your question about the mammalian PERK and ATF6 contributions, I regard the Mori and Walter credit as sound because the pathway concept, the IRE1 to HAC1 and XBP1 axis and the organelle-to-nucleus logic are theirs, and the later branches refine it. I do not support deferring B019. Sequencing only helps if the documentary check changes the answer, and nobody has said what evidence would be decisive. B002 loses nothing by waiting if the committee reaches it in a later year.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius argued that omitting Knudsen will be read as favouring academic discovery over development, and that a clinically obvious prize may also be the most open to a credit dispute.
responses.response: I agree that the criticism will be made and I think we should say openly why we accept it. The reading rests on the citation. If the prize is for the physiology and active forms of GLP-1, then recognising the discoverers follows from the wording, and Knudsen's work remains the demonstration that the biology could be turned into a drug. I do not think that is a principled argument for always preferring discovery. It is a judgment about this achievement, and for another one the same logic could point the other way. Your last point is the one I weigh most heavily: credit clarity belongs in the same assessment as clinical consequence, and that is why B002 is my first fallback.

uncertainties: The documentary record on who first showed the biological activity of GLP-1(7-36) and who first synthesized it. I cannot establish it from the supplied material, so Mojsov's place relative to the Habener group rests on recollection and the candidate record.
Whether the committee can accept the Knudsen exclusion openly without the prize being read as a verdict on the importance of drug development.

Whether B002 should overtake B019 if the committee decides that attribution reliability outweighs demonstrated clinical impact; my threshold is evidence that Mojsov's claim is no stronger than the competing one.
Long-term safety and durability of incretin therapy, including weight-loss maintenance, are still being characterized.
statement.conflict_note: No documented tie to Drucker, Holst, Knudsen or Mojsov, nor to Mori, Walter or any B004 candidate. As in round 1, I disclose about twenty co-authored works with committee member Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy) and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard. Neither involves a shortlisted candidate and I see no ground for recusal. As chair, I summarized round 1 and I have tried to keep that role separate from my own scientific judgment.
